RETRIEVE · EXPLAIN · CHECK · RETRY

Student revision

Find a weak topic, explain it without notes, check your reasoning and try a changed case later.

2026 foundation · 2027 revisions. Syllabus-linked requirement checklists use the textbook's source-demand review and item-level syllabus matrix. They are concise paraphrases, not official SCSA wording. Source editions · Official course and syllabuses.

Requirements, practice goals and extensions are different. Source-linked checkboxes summarise syllabus demands; chapter goals can include local teaching choices. Extensions have separate labels. A checklist tick or quiz score is a self-check, not teacher verification, full syllabus coverage or a grade prediction.

Offline revision workbookExplained answers

Markdown (.md) downloads are text documents. Print the visible section or use the downloads offline. Expand answers you want printed. Checklist ticks stay in this browser when storage is available; quiz answers stay only in the current page and are lost on refresh. No work is sent to the site.

Study explained examples

Topic checklists and retrieval

Tick a point only after an unaided explanation or changed practical attempt. Retain evidence elsewhere and revisit it after a gap. Requirement labels summarise related syllabus demands; the matrix retains the detailed source scope. Some requirements span several chapters.

Cumulative quizzes

Each successive cumulative set adds later units to earlier retrieval. The six sets draw from one bank of 32 questions, so questions repeat across sets and attempts. Use the explanations to diagnose a misconception; repeated scores are not fresh evidence of mastery. These multiple-choice quizzes do not replace written explanations or practical work.

Exam questions have one home

Study explained examples or choose timed practice from the same question bank.

Keep supporting extensions separate

These can deepen understanding or support a local project. They do not automatically add syllabus requirements. If your teacher includes one in an issued task, use the stated teaching and assessment scope.

SUPPORT BOOKLET + ENRICHMENT CONTEXT

LEFT JOIN extension and support-booklet HAVING

HAVING is shown in the official support booklet (printed p22), after GROUP BY. LEFT JOIN is additional to the explicitly listed INNER JOIN work. Do not label both optional-only or treat support-booklet examples as a separate new unit-content list; teach the relevant technique before assessment.

Open supporting practice

Optional retrieval

Why can COUNT(*) show one for an unmatched left-side row?

Explained support answer

The outer join preserves one row with NULL child fields. COUNT(child_key) instead counts non-NULL matches.

SUPPORT / IMPLEMENTATION / ENRICHMENT CONTEXT

Explicit SQLite transaction control

ACID and the role of database transactions remain syllabus-linked Year 12 requirements. This supporting lab adds explicit BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK syntax in a chosen SQLite tool; those commands are not an extra prescribed keyword list. Teach the chosen tool/driver behaviour before requiring the implementation locally.

Open supporting practice

Optional retrieval

Does an ordinary statement error always undo earlier statements automatically?

Explained support answer

No. Recovery depends on the DBMS/error and transaction boundary. Use an explicit, tested rollback strategy for the logical operation.

SUPPORT / IMPLEMENTATION / ENRICHMENT CONTEXT

Drone, VR and network-pod contexts

Optional delivery contexts. Specialist equipment and vendor-specific procedures are not general textbook prerequisites.

Open supporting practice

Optional retrieval

How can a learner practice a network-policy decision without a network pod?

Explained support answer

Apply the same declared rules to supplied request cards and predict outcomes. Label this as a model, not evidence of an executed network configuration.

SUPPORT / IMPLEMENTATION / ENRICHMENT CONTEXT

Additional computer-systems context

CPU pipeline and recorder-buffer examples in the activity pack are supporting context; they are not automatically additional examinable content. Binary/character representation remains in the syllabus-linked chapter material.

Open supporting practice

Optional retrieval

A recorder produces 9 MB/s and writes 6 MB/s. How quickly does an initially empty 24 MB buffer fill?

Explained support answer

It grows by 3 MB/s and fills after 24 / 3 = 8 seconds under the stated constant-rate assumptions.
